points.label: Former relation
points.left: Peace, suffering, love, and reconciliation. Romans 5:1–11 belongs to Gospel, Israel, and shared life.
points.right: Reconciliation becomes message and entrusted appeal. 2 Corinthians 5:18–21 belongs to Corinth and contested apostleship.

points.label: Entrusted message and action
points.left: Peace, suffering, love, and reconciliation. Being therefore justified by faith, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ; Not only so, but we also rejoice in God through our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom we have now received the reconciliation.
points.right: Reconciliation becomes message and entrusted appeal. But all things are of God, who reconciled us to himself through Jesus Christ, and gave to us the ministry of reconciliation; For him who knew no sin he made to be sin on our behalf, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God.

payload.tension: Reconciliation in Romans and Corinth places two independently valuable sources together while preserving their distinct audience, form, sequence, and stated purpose.
